See the fields and rendering equation

I = g [ T J + (1 − T) A ]

Computed in linear RGB. The clean training target is gJ, not the unadjusted background J.

T and A are effective image-space quantities, not unique physical measurements of smoke density or depth.

A learned transfer control

Preserving the background matters.

The supplementary experiment retrains PHATNet’s transfer network on the training recordings and transfers onto the same clean targets. Measured renders better preserve clear content in the fire-domain restoration comparison.

The transfer network is retrained on the training recordings; these results do not use the released PHATNet dehazing checkpoint. On RealX3D, the full model scores 18.19 dB and the PHATNet + SmokeBench setting scores 18.32 dB; the advantage is not universal. Supplementary Sec. S9.

Semantic Rectification

A frozen DINOv3 ViT-L/16 encoder supplies semantic features at blocks 6, 12, 18 and 24. FireDesmoke rectifies its smoke-degraded tokens and fuses them with an AdaIR pixel branch to restore a single RGB input.

The parallel restoration branches are shown in the method overview.

Closer to clean-view features

Dense smoke strongly changes deep tokens. Rectification improves their similarity, but does not fully recover the clean representation.

Mean cosine similarity · 1,000 test frames · Supplementary Sec. S9. Clean-view tokens are used for this analysis and training supervision, not inference.

Limitations

Residual smoke & colour shifts

Near-opaque smoke can remain. The method does not guarantee reconstruction of invisible objects.

Transfer is not universal

On RealX3D, FireDesmoke has higher image-average PSNR than GenDeg (18.19 vs. 17.94 dB), while GenDeg has higher SSIM (0.715 vs. 0.712). A darker or clearer-looking output is not automatically more consistent with the reference.

Scope of the fire evidence

The held-out burns are from a different viewpoint at the same facility. Chamber smoke is mostly light or absent, so that test mainly checks preservation rather than dense-smoke removal.
